etymologies.etymologyHTML: Originally "meet, meet in argument", borrowed from Middle French occurrer, from Latin occurrō (“run to meet, run against, befall, present itself”) from prefix ob- (“against”) + verb currō (“run, hurry, move”).

quote.citation: 1959, Georgette Heyer, chapter 1, in The Unknown Ajax:
quote.text: And no use for anyone to tell Charles that this was because the Family was in mourning for Mr Granville Darracott […]: Charles might only have been second footman at Darracott Place for a couple of months when that disaster occurred, but no one could gammon him into thinking that my lord cared a spangle for his heir.

definitions.definition: (impersonal) To come or be presented to the mind; to suggest itself.

quote.citation: 1995, Theodore Kaczynski, Industrial Society and Its Future:
quote.text: Apparently it never occurs to them that you can't make rapid, drastic changes in the technology and the economy of a society without causing rapid changes in all other aspects of the society as well,  […]

definitions.definition: (intransitive, sciences) To be present or found.
